concepts.title: Every Leg Has to Land
concepts.rationale: A parlay ticket turns the all-or-nothing rule into a quick visual read. Its one-in-eight example states the independent 50/50-pick assumption used for the arithmetic.
concepts.caption: A parlay is one bet with several picks. Every leg has to win. With three independent 50/50 picks, that is one chance in eight. Read the whole ticket before the game starts.
concepts.alt: A Playbook social card with a three-pick parlay ticket. It says every leg has to land, every pick must win, and three independent picks with a true 50/50 chance each produce a one-in-eight chance that all three win.

sources.note: Supports that all picks must win. The card separately states its 0.5 × 0.5 × 0.5 = 1 in 8 independent-pick arithmetic assumption; it does not derive probability from a quoted price.

concepts.title: The Slot Does Not Have a Memory
concepts.rationale: A fading sequence of old spins makes the independence of the next result immediate. The visual gives the myth a concrete answer without scolding the player.
concepts.caption: A slot cannot be due. Each spin is independent, so past results cannot change the next one.
concepts.alt: A dark Playbook myth card reads The slot does not have a memory. Seven faded past spin markers sit above a bright label stating Next spin: same odds.

sources.note: Supports that each spin is generated independently and that a machine with 200 prior spins has the same odds on spin 201.

concepts.title: RTP Is the Long Game
concepts.rationale: A receipt-style calculation separates return to player from a session outcome. It turns the 95 percent RTP example into clear, visible long-run arithmetic.
concepts.caption: A 95% RTP describes a long-run average, not a promise for one session. The paytable is the place to start.
concepts.alt: A Playbook social card uses a receipt layout to explain a 95 percent slot return to player. It shows 100 dollars wagered over time, approximately 95 dollars paid back, and approximately 5 dollars as the house edge.

sources.section: What this means for your wallet
sources.note: Supports the 95% RTP and 5% house-edge example: for every $100 bet over time, about $5 is lost on average; a session may vary.

notes: Sports probability uses three independent picks, each with a true 50/50 chance: 0.5³ = 1 in 8. RTP is a long-run average and does not predict an individual session.
